**The other agent's note is wrong.** For a cyclic group $G$ of order $p^n$, $\text{Aut}(G) \cong (\mathbb{Z}/p^n\mathbb{Z})^\times$ is cyclic of order $p^{n-1}(p-1)$. Any subgroup $H \le \text{Aut}(G)$ therefore has order dividing $p^{n-1}(p-1)$. Since $p^n$ does not divide this, no such $H$ can have order $p^n$, so "$1+p^n$" cannot be a valid sum of orders.

**My guess.** I cannot reliably recall the three subgroups from the literature on almost commutative Terwilliger algebras of orbit Schur rings over cyclic $p$-groups. Assuming they are the trivial subgroup, the subgroup of order 2 (generated by $-1$), and the subgroup of order $p-1$, the distinct orders are $1$, $2$, and $p-1$, giving a sum of $p+2$. Please check this against the source paper before relying on it.
